As a result, life for a horse was pretty much appalling and life span was relatively short. Although the city designated places along the waterfront to dispose of carcasses many, like the one pictured, were simply left on the street where they fell.

Why did we move from suspenders, like in this image to wearing belts to keep our pants up?

After losing popularity during World War I, when men became accustomed to uniform belts, suspenders were still regular attire throughout the 1920s. Because of their image as 'underwear', some men switched to belts during the 1930s as the vests which had hidden suspenders became worn less often... Life magazine stated in 1938 that 60% of American men chose belts over suspenders.
